documents.title: An external view
documents.plain:
**Evidence: documented behavior; model abstraction.**

This small context interprets the article’s system boundaries. It omits internal storage and replication details.

Start here: the article describes Continuity, a Git storage system behind Origin. Local Git repositories are disposable warm caches; the S3 WAL is authoritative. Inspect Continuity, then follow its detail to logical containers. Use the Diagram key, Plain language and STE100 text controls; STE is a draft. Related views show separate push, read, gossip, rebuild and compaction stories. This is a reading model, not a running simulation.

documents.title: Logical container view
documents.plain:
**Evidence: inferred decomposition.**

This is an inferred C4 decomposition of the article’s responsibilities. A logical Continuity server uses a local Git repository and the external S3 WAL. It does not claim separate deployable services, host counts, or a production topology.

Rendezvous hashing ranks preferred healthy hosts from repository ID and node membership. It is a placement optimization, not a routing database or durable repository ownership. Drill into the server for inferred responsibilities.

documents.title: Push: durable publication
documents.plain:
**Evidence: documented behavior; model abstraction.**

Original abstraction: WAL persistence and local preparation precede CAS publication. Branches keep independent order; boundaries are inferred.

Local pack writing and WAL upload are concurrent branches; reference preparation follows the local write. Both branches precede CAS publication. These reading selections do not invent a total order or a lockstep barrier. Acknowledgement follows durable persistence. CAS conflicts may cause refetch and retry; that alternative is not simultaneously drawn as a successful publication.

ste.text:
Evidence: documented behavior; model abstraction.

Write the local pack and upload the WAL entry in separate branches. Prepare the references after the local write. Wait for both branches before CAS publication. Upload alone does not publish the push. Commit the local references. Then acknowledge the push. Do not read branch identifiers as a total order. A CAS conflict can require a retry; that alternative is not part of this successful path.

documents.title: Compaction: reuse compacted packs
documents.plain:
**Evidence: documented behavior; model abstraction.**

Only the primary compacts; replicas follow the WAL and reuse the result. Role boundaries are inferred.

The primary compacts both on-disk data and WAL history. Replicas reuse compacted packs, trading bandwidth for CPU. This sequence abstracts dependencies, not measured timing.

ste.text:
Evidence: documented behavior; model abstraction.

The primary compacts the data. The replica gets the compacted packs.

documents.title: Illustrative deployment

**Evidence: illustrative.**

This topology is hypothetical. It demonstrates nested hosts, distinct server replicas, a cache, and durable storage. The article supports the logical roles and S3 durability. It does not establish the host count, regions, replica placement, process boundaries, or implementation language shown here. Collapsing a host hides its descendants and their relationships; no ancestor relationship is invented.

Follow a replica link to the logical server detail. Collapse a host to hide its children and their relationships. The model does not create relationships for hidden endpoints.

documents.title: Rebuild a disposable cache
documents.plain: **Evidence: documented behavior; inferred reading sequence.** If a local repository is absent, Continuity materializes it from the WAL. Rendezvous hashing chooses preferred healthy nodes; a changed ranking does not make a discarded cache authoritative. This story does not specify recovery time or a real machine count.

ste.text:
Evidence: documented behavior; model abstraction.

If the local repository is absent, rebuild it from the WAL. Then serve the request. Preferred nodes can change. The WAL remains the source of truth.
